title_content.content: Site-Selective Direct γ-Difunctionalization of Diazoenals: Application to the Synthesis of Enal-Functionalized Allenes and Furans

paragraph_content.content: Jagadeesh Kalepu,<sup>[a]</sup> Bapurao Sudam Lad<sup>+</sup>,<sup>[a]</sup> Pratap Kumar Mandal<sup>+</sup>,<sup>[a]</sup> Vinaykumar Kanchupalli<sup>+</sup>,<sup>[a]</sup> Durjay Roy,<sup>[a]</sup> and Sreenivas Katukojvala*<sup>[a]</sup>

A new approach for the synthetically important γ-functionalized enals has been developed. The strategy involves rhodiumcatalyzed direct C�C & C�S bond forming site-selective γ- difunctionalization of diazoenals with aryl propargyl sulfides via sulfur ylide [2,3] sigmatropic rearrangement, resulting in the highly functionalized γ-allenyl(sulfanyl)enals in excellent yield at ambient temperature. Enals are important building blocks in chemical synthesis and continue to be vital substrates for the development of organocatalysis.<sup>[1–2]</sup> However, despite the enormous synthetic utility, very few catalytic methods are available for the γ- functionalization of enals. The direct site-selective γ-functionalization of unmodified enals has been challenging.<sup>[3–7]</sup> So far, the known approaches relies on the remote carbonyl-directed γ- functionalization via the electron-rich dienyl motifs such as Mukaiyama dienolsilylethers,<sup>[3]</sup> metal-dienolates<sup>[4]</sup> and dienamines (Scheme 1A).<sup>[5,6]</sup> However, these approaches often suffer from the competitive α-functionalization and cycloaddition pathways of the conformationally labile 4-carbon dienyl motif.<sup>[5,8,9]</sup> Therefore, given the limitations associated with the existing strategies, the development of general, efficient, and operationally simple new catalytic approaches to the synthetically useful γ-functionalized enals would be highly valuable.

Metal carbenes derived from diazo compounds are valuable reactive intermediates that are central to a wide range of carbene transfer reactions such as σ-bond insertions (C�H, C�X, and X�H; X = heteroatom), cycloadditions, and ylide rearrangement reactions.<sup>[10,11]</sup> In particular, the ability of carbenoids to offer geminal difunctionalization through acceptor/donor reactivity provides rapid molecular complexity. The synthetic utility of the γ- allenyl(sulfanyl)enals was demonstrated by the InCl -catalyzed cycloisomerization to the trisubstituted furanyl-enals via an unusual 1,4-sulfanyl migration. In addition, an operationally simple and efficient one-pot [3+ 2] annulation of diazoenals and propargyl sulfides, involving combined γ-difunctionalization and cycloisomerization was successfully developed for the diverse enal-functionalized furans.

paragraph_content.content: In continuation of our ongoing studies on the synthetic applications of diazoenals,<sup>[12–15]</sup> we recently reported the siteselective γ-amination via enalcarbenoid NH-insertion reaction with propargyl amine. The resulting donor-acceptor dienamine intermediates were successfully utilized in the construction of valuable enal-functionalized 1,4-oxazine heterocycles.<sup>[13]</sup> Inspired by these studies, we next examined the carbene transfer reaction of diazoenal 1 a and phenyl propargyl sulfide 2 a anticipating C�S & C�C bond forming direct γ-difunctionalization through the sulfur ylide [2,3] sigmatropic rearrangement.<sup>[16]</sup> Gratifyingly, a variety of dirhodium carboxylates such as Rh (OAc) , Rh (oct) , Rh (tfa) and Rh (esp) efficiently catalyzed the reaction producing γ-quaternized γ-allenyl(sulfanyl)enal 3 in 85–95 % yield (Table 1, entries 1–4). The bulky chiral Rh {(S)- DOSP} required longer reaction time and gave allene 3 in reduced yield (65%) with the marginal enantioselectivity (5 % ee). The best yield was obtained with 1 mol % Rh (OAc) at ambient conditions (95 %, entry 1). The reaction was compatible with other halogenated solvents, and toluene, whereas oxygenated solvents are not compatible (See SI for full optimization table).

paragraph_content.content: With the optimized conditions (Table 1, entry 1) the scope of the γ-difunctionalization was examined with various diazoenals and aryl propargyl sulfides (Table 2). Though the electronic nature of the aryl substituent of diazoenal does not have much effect on the reaction (3–8: 81–97%), sterically hindered 2-bromoaryl and thiophene groups hampered the yields (9–10: 63–68 %). Among the aryl propargyl sulfides, a variety of electronically distinct aryl substituents such as alkyl-, halo- (F, Cl, Br), methoxy-, and nitro- groups were well tolerated to give excellent yields of the corresponding allenyl-enals (11– 31: 85–98%). The scope of the [3 +2] annulation involving γ-difunctionalization/cycloisomerization was investigated with diverse enaldiazo ketones 1 and aryl propargyl sulfides 2 (Table 4). Excellent yields of furans 33–37 (87–94%) were obtained with alkyl, halo, and oxygenated aryl enaldiazo ketones indicating that reaction is not sensitive to the electronic nature of the aryl ring. However, the sterically hindered 2-Br aryl and heteroaryl thiophene substituted diazoenal hampered the reaction (38–39, 56–58 %). In case of aryl propargyl sulfides, diverse alkyl-, halo-, and methoxy-substitutions on the aryl ring are well tolerated leading to the furans 40–63 in excellent yield (86–96%). Whereas electron-withdrawing nitro-group resulted in slightly diminished yield of furans 64–65 (77–79%). With respect to the steric influence, the 2-methyl, 2-halo-, and 2-methoxy aryl sulfides also smoothly participated in the reaction (40–42, 46– 51, and 60).

To understand the mechanism of the furan formation, a series of control experiments were carried out (Scheme 2). A 1: 1 mixture of allene 7 and 15 was subjected to the rearrangement reaction in the presence of 3 mol % InCl . Interestingly, in addition to the anticipated furans 36 and 43, the reaction also produced considerable amounts of crossed furan products 44 and 32 through intermolecular sulfide migration (Scheme 2A). Performing the cycloisomerization of allene 7 in the presence of 4-methylthiophenol 66 produced furan 36 along with the crossed furan 44 in about a 2 : 1 ratio (Scheme 2B). Further, a large-scale cycloisomerization reaction of 7 led to the detection of a trace amount of diphenyl disulfide 67 (Scheme 2C). However, treating furan 36 with 4-methylthiophenol 66 in the presence of InCl failed to produce the crossed furan 44 (Scheme 2D), indicating that sulfanyl migration is irreversible.

Based on the control experiments, a plausible mechanism for the [3 + 2] annulation via γ-difunctionalization and cycloisomerization reaction, involving Rh(II) and In(III) catalytic cycles is depicted in Scheme 3. The Rh-enalcarbenoid 68 derived from diazoenal 1 reacts with propargyl sulfide 2 to give sulfonium ylide 69A. Subsequent [2,3] sigmatropic rearrangement of 69A or the metal-free ylide 69 B leads to the γ-allenyl(sulfanyl)enal 70. The low enantioselectivity

observed for Table 1, entry 5 may support the metal free ylide rearrangement. In the In-catalysis, intramolecular allylic sulfide displacement via 5- endo-dig heterocyclization of In(III) activated allenyl sulfide 71 results in the unstable 2-methylene-2H-furan-1-ium and Indiumthiolate ion pair 72. The involvement of this ion pair intermediate supports the results of the control experiments (Scheme 2). Finally, the recombination of ion pair 72 by the thiolate nucleophilic addition completes the 1,4-sulfanyl migration<sup>[21]</sup> and furnishes the enal-functionalized furan product 73. Notably, the overall annulation reaction involves only
as the by-product.

The synthetic utility of the furanyl-enal 35 was demonstrated by further transformations (Scheme 4). Chemoselective oxidation using m-CPBA, gave a mixture of sulfone 74 and sulfoxide 75 in 76 % and 22 % yield respectively.<sup>[22]</sup>. The structure of 74 has been confirmed by the single crystal X-ray diffraction. Olefination of furanyl-enal 35 with phosphorane 76 produced the valuable dienone-tethered furan 77 in 81 % yield.
In summary, we have developed a new approach for the synthetically important γ-difunctionalized enals. The strategy involves rhodium-catalyzed direct
\mathsf { C } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { C } \ \& \ \mathsf { C } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { S }

bond forming site-selective γ-difunctionalization of diazoenals with aryl propargyl sulfides via sulfur ylide [2,3] sigmatropic rearrangement and provides functionally rich γ-allenyl(sulfanyl)enals in excellent yield at ambient temperature. The synthetic utility of the new enals was demonstrated by the InCl -catalyzed cycloisomerization to the trisubstituted furanyl-enals via an unusual 1,4-sulfanyl migration. Moreover, an operationally simple and efficient one-opt [3 + 2] annulation of diazoenals and aryl propargyl sulfides gave diverse enal-functionalized furans. Further study on the synthetic applications of γ-difinctionalization and [3+2] annulation is ongoing.
